trust_decision.summary: A side-band packet whose payload, after the band byte, is empty or attacker-chosen must be decoded without indexing past its bounds; this is decided in PacketLineRef::decode_band and TextRef::from in gix-packetline, which every remote progress/error band goes through.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'empty side-band packet', and decode_band's unchecked d[0] is the first band-decoding code an engineer reads; the real wire trigger (packet 0005 + band 2/3 giving an empty payload) actually panics one step later in TextRef::from at lib.rs:199.

fix_sites.entry_point: WithSidebands BufRead/Read (blocking and async) via gix-transport ExtendedBufRead set_progress_handler, which gix-protocol fetch uses (gix clone/fetch); also public TextRef::from / PacketLineRef::as_text
fix_sites.module_kind: core decoding type (shared by blocking and async)

fix_sites.entry_point: public API PacketLineRef::decode_band; called from WithSidebands::fill_buf / poll_fill_buf
StreamingPeekableIter::read_line / peek_line (blocking); defensive only, because buf is always resized to MAX_LINE_LEN first (read.rs:141-142, 168)
StreamingPeekableIter::read_line / peek_line (async); defensive only, buf resized at async_io/read.rs:146,173

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: gix-packetline/src/async_io/sidebands.rs:292-298 (async copy of the blocking sideband loop). The fix covers it only indirectly, by fixing the shared TextRef::from at gix-packetline/src/lib.rs:199

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who guards the empty payload inside blocking_io/sidebands.rs:155/161 (the client path most users hit) can argue the async-io feature is a separate, non-default transport; and if they fix only decode_band (the 'empty packet' in the summary), they can argue TextRef::from is a plain text helper, not sideband decoding.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Empty progress/error bands (keep-alive packets under sideband-all) must still be forwarded to the progress handler with empty text rather than rejected. The fix's test checks this, and translate_to_progress depends on it. Also, empty Data bands are skipped, not treated as errors.

O6_input_shapes: Data line with no bytes at all, so no band id (decode_band d[0]) — public-API only, because the wire decoder rejects length 0004 (gix-packetline/src/decode.rs:83-85)
band 2 (progress) with an empty payload: packet 0005\x02
band 3 (error) with an empty payload: packet 0005\x03
buffer shorter than 4 bytes given to read_line_inner (defensive)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a capability-line parser that strips a trailing newline or reads the first byte by index on server text lines
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handshake parses server text lines byte by byte, and a maintainer could easily write line[line.len()-1] there; it is in a different crate from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a progress parser that indexes the byte after ':' or the first byte of action without a length check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits downstream of the same sideband payload in another package; the current code uses position/strip_prefix safely, but an indexed version would be natural to write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: HTTP smart-protocol service-announcement line parsing with indexed newline stripping
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a second transport (HTTP) that reads server text lines on its own code path.

O9_family: integer underflow / out-of-bounds slice index leading to a panic (CWE-191) when decoding network packet lines

O10_build.toolchain: cargo (stable; workspace crate gix-packetline with blocking-io / async-io features)
O10_build.project_tests: gix-packetline/tests (decode/mod.rs, read/sideband.rs using maybe_async for both blocking-io and async-io), plus the fuzz target gix-packetline/fuzz/fuzz_targets/packet_lines.rs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a d.is_empty() check in decode_band only, or reject empty progress/error bands with an error (which breaks sideband-all keep-alives), leaving TextRef::from's d[d.len()-1] underflow in place.

out_of_scope_notes: gix-transport/src/client/blocking_io/request.rs:86 and gix-transport/src/client/async_io/request.rs:94 call TextRef::from on caller-supplied write data; this is a local API, not the network, and the shared lib.rs fix covers it anyway.
The read_line_inner buffer-length guards (fix.diff:14-18, 32-36) cannot be reached through public API at the pinned commit; they are pure hardening.
